Facturation conforme (référence de dossier, transparence des prix appliqués). title: Framework for Call-down Technical Assistance - Engineering and Climate-Resilient Infrastructure Advisory Services (BRAVE-IS)
description: DAI Global UK is seeking proposals from firms or consortia to provide engineering and climate-resilient infrastructure advisory services to the Building Resilience and Addressing Vulnerability to Emergencies - Institutional Strengthening (BRAVE-IS) programme in Pakistan. BRAVE-IS is a multi-year (2026-2029) technical assistance programme funded by the UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO). Background Pakistan's infrastructure is highly exposed to floods, extreme heat, drought, landslides and earthquakes. Government has introduced climate and disaster risk requirements into public investment planning, but institutions need specialist engineering support to apply them in how infrastructure is planned, designed, appraised and maintained. Scope BRAVE-IS will appoint a firm or consortium under a Time and Materials call-down framework, from which it can mobilise engineering experts and, where needed, complete delivery teams. Work will be commissioned through individual task requests. Expertise is required in: climate-resilient infrastructure engineering and design; hydrology, hydraulics and flood-risk engineering; water resources, irrigation and drainage; infrastructure planning, appraisal and risk assessment; geospatial, digital and engineering software; and engineering institutional strengthening and capacity development. Support must strengthen, not substitute for, government capacity. Eligibility Applicants must be legally registered in Pakistan and hold valid Pakistan Engineering Council (PEC) registration as a consulting engineering firm. Consortia of up to four members are welcome, led by a single lead member. Personnel will work in Islamabad, Lahore, Karachi, Peshawar and Gilgit, with travel elsewhere in Pakistan as required, and rates are sought for locally based personnel. Contract The initial period runs from date of award to 31 March 2027, extendable subject to programme requirements, performance and FCDO approval. Contracts will be issued by DAI Pakistan (Pvt.) Ltd. No minimum volume of work is guaranteed. How to apply Submit one email to brave-is@dai.com with the subject line "BRAVE-IS-003 - Proposal - [Firm name]", attaching two separate PDF files: (1) a technical submission of no more than ten pages, with CVs as an annex, and (2) a financial proposal giving daily fee rates only for five personnel levels. Proposals will be scored 80% technical and 20% financial and must remain valid for 90 days. Key dates Clarification questions: by 29 October 2026, by email to brave-is@dai.com with the subject line "BRAVE-IS-003 - Clarification Question - [Firm name]". All questions and responses will be published on Contracts Finder. Proposal deadline: 9 November 2026, 17:00 Pakistan Standard Time (12:00 UK time). Please read the full RFP (reference BRAVE-IS-003) before applying. Late submissions will not be considered. DAI reserves the right to cancel the procurement or make no award.

title: Provision of Motor Control Centres, Systems Integration and ICA Services
description:
Scottish Water is seeking to establish a multi-supplier Framework Agreement for the provision of Motor Control Centres (MCCs), Instrumentation, Control and Automation (ICA), Systems Integration (SI) and ICA maintenance and support services. The Framework will provide a flexible, scalable and resilient route to market for electrical, control, automation and Operational Technology (OT) requirements across Scottish Water's water and wastewater assets, supporting capital delivery, asset renewal and operational requirements.

The Framework will be divided into three Lots, with multiple suppliers appointed to each Lot: Lot 1 – Integrated MCC, ICA and Systems Integration; Lot 2 – Systems Integration and Automation Services; and Lot 3 – ICA Maintenance, Minor Works and Support. Suppliers may apply for one, several or all Lots. Depending on the nature, value, complexity and risk of each requirement, call-offs may be for fully integrated end-to-end solutions, standalone equipment supply or discrete specialist services. The Framework will be available for use by Scottish Water and its appointed Delivery Vehicles.

Call-off contracts may be awarded by direct award or by mini-competition between the suppliers appointed to the relevant Lot(s), in accordance with the Framework Agreement. Scottish Water gives no guarantee of the volume or value of work to be called off under the Framework or any Lot. The estimated value stated in the Contract Notice is the maximum anticipated value over the full Framework term and is indicative only.

The Framework will be based on NEC4 terms. Call-off contracts may be placed under the NEC4 Professional Service Short Contract, the NEC4 Engineering and Construction Short Contract or Scottish Water Purchase Order Conditions, as appropriate to the requirement and Lot being engaged.

Suppliers must maintain all relevant certifications, standards and regulatory compliance throughout the Framework term. MCC assemblies must comply with the current edition of the BS EN IEC 61439 series, including Parts 1 and 2. As a designated Operator of Essential Services, Scottish Water will require suppliers to support its obligations under the Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations, including secure-by-design engineering, OT cyber security controls, vulnerability management, personnel assurance and cyber assurance activities. Suppliers must be able to work safely within live operational environments forming part of Critical National Infrastructure, and bidders will be assessed on their capability to undertake the relevant CDM duty holder role(s) for each Lot.

Scottish Water is seeking suppliers who will work collaboratively as long-term delivery partners, including early engagement in project development, design and buildability reviews, accurate lead time and pipeline information, and support for standardisation, innovation, whole-life value and carbon reduction. Performance will be managed through key performance indicators, regular reporting and continuous improvement.

It is estimated the Framework Agreement will start in April 2027 and run for an initial term of 6 years. Scottish Water may extend it by up to 3 further periods of 2 years each. The maximum duration, including all extensions, is 12 years, ending March 2039. Scottish Water may use each extension at its discretion, depending on supplier performance, continued value for money and business needs.

title: Belgium – Company health services – La fourniture d’un service externe pour la prévention et la protection au travail (SEPPT).
description: La fourniture d’un service externe pour la prévention et la protection au travail (SEPPT), tel que prévu par la loi et le Code du bien-être au travail. Il sera fait appel au SEPPT pour la surveillance de la santé de notre personnel (y compris les attestations médicales et psychologiques dans le cadre de la réglementation ferroviaire), la gestion des risques (y compris les interventions psychosociales formelles), les visites des lieux de travail et d’autres services relevant des 7 domaines du bien-être prévus par la législation. Un élément important dans le cadre du présent marché est que la collaboration est également soumise à des dispositions légales spécifiques. Compte tenu de la nature et de l’ampleur des activités de la SNCB, l’accent de la future mission portera sur le volet médical, en particulier la surveillance de la santé. Environ 80 % des membres du personnel exercent une fonction de sécurité telle que définie dans la législation relative au bien-être, tandis qu’environ 50 % exercent une fonction de sécurité ferroviaire. Pour les fonctions de sécurité ferroviaire, telles que les conducteurs de train, les accompagnateurs de train et d’autres fonctions comportant des tâches critiques pour la sécurité, les attestations requises ne peuvent être délivrées que par un centre médico-psychologique agréé par le SSICF. Le futur fournisseur devra dès lors disposer d’un tel agrément ou être disposé à l’obtenir. En moyenne, environ 15 900 examens médicaux et psychologiques sont réalisés chaque année. Cela comprend notamment les examens périodiques, les examens spéciaux, les attestations médicales et psychologiques conformément à la réglementation ferroviaire, les examens préalables à l’embauche et les examens en cas de changement de poste de travail. Vous trouverez ci-dessous une indication du nombre des différents examens réalisés par an : Examens périodiques 8.500 / Examens spéciaux (consultations spontanées, RIT, visite préalable,…) 2.900 / Attestations médicales (conformément à la réglementation ferroviaire) 2.700 / Attestations psychologiques (conformément à la réglementation ferroviaire) 500 / Examens préalables (embauche + changement de poste de travail) 1.300 / TOTAL 15.900 / Étant donné que les activités de la SNCB sont réparties sur l’ensemble du territoire belge, le futur prestataire de services doit être en mesure d’organiser le service au niveau national, tant en néerlandais qu’en français. La préférence est donnée à une prestation de services dans les bâtiments de la SNCB ou dans des lieux situés à proximité d’un bâtiment de gare et/ou facilement accessibles en train. Une spécificité supplémentaire concerne la combinaison de membres du personnel statutaires et contractuels. Pour les membres du personnel statutaires, un statut spécifique et une réglementation du personnel spécifique sont applicables, à savoir le RGPS, ce qui suppose que le prestataire de services puisse aligner sa prestation sur ceux ci. En outre, l’intégration des données entre les systèmes du prestataire de services et SAP constitue une exigence dans le cadre de la future collaboration. Compte tenu de la complexité de la mission, de l’intégration, du besoin de continuité et de la sensibilité des données, il est actuellement envisagé de prévoir un marché d’une durée de 8 ans. Dans le cadre de la présente procédure de passation, la SNCB agit en tant que centrale d’achat au sens de l’article 2, 6°, b), de la loi du 17/06/2016 relative aux marchés publics, exerçant des activités d’achat centralisées et auxiliaires au sens de l’article 2, 7°, b), et ce pour les filiales de la SNCB, telles qu’Ypto.

title: Access Control and Intrusion Detection Services
description: The Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) requires the provision of parts and labour (technical support, programming, installation, service, and maintenance) on an “as and when requested” basis for its Integrated Security System (ISS) at CRA locations across Canada. The CRA is considering the conversion of up to 51 sites currently using a combination of Digital Security Controls (DSC) Intrusion Detection Systems and Kantech Access Control systems to a unified Kantech Intrusion/Access Control platform. The site counts identified below represent the CRA’s current intended conversion plans for planning and estimation purposes only and do not constitute a commitment to convert any specific number of sites. Ontario – up to 13 sites identified for potential conversion; 3. Quebec – up to 1 site identified for potential conversion; 4. Atlantic – up to 4 sites identified for potential conversion; and 5. Western – up to 22 sites identified for potential conversion. Bidders may submit a bid for one (1) or more Regions identified in this RFP. Only one (1) bid submission is required, regardless of the number of Regions for which the Bidder is submitting a bid. The Bidder's submission must clearly identify each Region for which it is proposing to provide the required goods and services. For each Region bid, the Bidder must provide all information required by this RFP, including any Region-specific technical information, resource information, and pricing, in the format prescribed in the bid solicitation documents. Where a Bidder fails to meet a Region-specific requirement, the CRA may declare the bid non-responsive for that Region only. For greater certainty, a determination that a bid is non-responsive for one (1) Region will not, in itself, render the Bidder's submission non-responsive for any other Region for which a bid as been submitted, provided all applicable requirements for those Regions are met. The CRA intends to award up to five (5) contracts to fulfill this requirement. A Bidder may be awarded a contract for one (1) Region, multiple Regions, or all five (5) Regions. The period of the resulting contract(s) will be for three (3) firm years. The contract(s) will include four (4) irrevocable one-year options to extend the period of the contract(s). For each Region, the responsive bid with the highest combined rating of technical merit and price will be recommended for award of a contract. Each Region will be evaluated separately. title: Real Time Spectrum Analyzer
description: The National Research Council Canada has a requirement for the supply of a 1.2 GHz acquisition bandwidth real-time spectrum analyzer (26.5 GHz) to capture and stream in-phase and quadrature (I/Q) data. The real-time spectrum analyzer will be used in a reverberation chamber to qualify DUTs against very stringent telescope protection levels. To achieve this, a low-noise, ultra-sensitive real-time spectrum analyzer is required. The real-time spectrum analyzer will capture and stream I/Q data that is used to reconstruct complex time domain signals that are then transformed to the frequency domain where radio astronomy techniques of spectral integration are used to reduce the standard deviation of the noise.
